brief: UBS forecasts 28% EPS growth for the S&P 500's September quarter, driven by AI-related capex (estimated +84% to USD900bn) pushing semiconductor profits to about half of Q3 earnings growth and cloud revenue growth accelerating to 58% y/y from 48% in the June quarter. Nine straight months of ISM new-orders expansion, historically lasting about three years, broadens growth to cyclicals, while initial jobless claims near multi-decade lows support consumer spending despite elevated energy costs. The 10-year yield's rise of over 1 percentage point poses manageable refinancing risk given the index's roughly 11-year average debt maturity, so UBS recommends diversified cyclical and secular equity exposure. Separately, a Wall Street-led semiconductor selloff hit Asia (Samsung -7.4%, SK Hynix -10.1%, Nikkei -1.8%, Taiwan -2%) on memory-competition and AI-financing concerns, but UBS stays positive on Asian equities, sees limits to further dollar strength, and favors select tech names plus opportunities in Japan, India, Singapore and China A-shares. NY Fed's Williams said one more 2026 hike may fit but sees no case for further 2027 moves and called the labor market balanced; UBS's base case keeps the Fed on hold until December, with Wednesday's CPI print as the key test of that path.
